research_question: after a large event, does entering only once price has actually shown a direction produce an edge after VIP0 taker cost, without being too late and while filtering enough false directions?

methodology_change.reason: D5.4 entered at the shock and was a coin flip: C2 stopped 104 times and hit target 104 times, with event displacement 12 to 15 times the round-trip cost. The failure was absence of direction information at the event instant, not insufficient movement or excessive fees.

event_source.name: SHOCK
event_source.inherited_from: D5.4 E1 detector, C1 and C2 unioned; thresholds unchanged
event_source.single_source_rationale: the variable under test is the confirmation logic; three candidates sharing one event set isolates it

excluded.E2: already rejected at the D5.4 cost-first stage; reintroduction banned
excluded.E3: overlapping volatility condition would not give an independent comparison
excluded.E4: a subset of E1 conditions; not an independent comparison

shock_window.why_not_event_bars_only: the event run is a median of 3 bars and its range is 54bp, a third of the displacement; a margin built on it would be 1.2x cost and would not filter

confirmation_common.window_rationale: four times the 15 minute shock window; 30m leaves A and C near the sample floor, 120m stops filtering (A 42.9%, C 75.2%)
confirmation_common.min_margin_rationale: 2x round-trip cost; anything narrower is not distinguishable from noise

candidates.name: SHOCK_BREAKOUT_CONTINUATION
candidates.hypothesis: leaving the shock range by a meaningful margin says the flow that made the shock is not finished; the breakout names the direction, the event does not
candidates.stop: the broken level (H for LONG, L for SHORT)
candidates.k_selection: ladder {0.15, 0.25, 0.40} fixed in advance; at 0.15 17.1% of events fall back on the cost floor so the range-proportional rule stops binding, at 0.25 that share is 0.5%

candidates.name: SHOCK_RETRACEMENT_CONFIRMATION
candidates.hypothesis: half the shock retraced means the forced flow has ended and normalisation is actually underway; D5.4 entered at the extreme, this enters once half the move is back
candidates.stop: the shock extreme (L for LONG, H for SHORT)
candidates.k_selection: 0.5 is the standard half retracement and the middle of the ladder {0.382, 0.5, 0.618}
candidates.discarded_definition: a bounce of k off the running low confirmed 99.0% of the time and was not a filter; replaced with a retracement measured from P0. Changed on confirmation frequency alone, never on returns.

candidates.name: POST_SHOCK_COMPRESSION_EXPANSION
candidates.stage_2: compression range CH/CL over the 15 bars ending at that bar
candidates.hypothesis: shock, digestion, resolution: a breakout after volatility has halved says the market has chosen a direction
candidates.compression_selection: 0.5 states that volatility halved; not searched

exits.reason: D5.4's symmetric bracket was a coin flip; A and C deliberately have no target so the continuation hypothesis has open upside

intrabar.stop_fill: min(stop, bar open) for LONG, max for SHORT
intrabar.target_fill: max(target, bar open) for LONG, min for SHORT

costs.funding: actual D2 rates on the 8h UTC grid, engine applied

SURVIVE.rule: OOS VIP0_BASE net mean > 0 and 95% CI lower bound > 0
sample gate satisfied: events >= 200, confirmed trades >= 60, 5 years, evaluable folds >= 5
judgeable folds: gross>0 in >= 2/3, net>0 in >= 1/2
no single trade > 20% of total net sum

verdict_rules.S10_rationale: D5.4 found no direction information at the event instant; if confirmation supplied it, fewer than half the trades should end at the stop. This measures whipsaw directly.
verdict_rules.WEAK: S1 passes, at least one other fails

d6_v2_gate.even_then: design -> implementation -> historical -> shadow -> AUTO paper

liquidation_future.future_role: confirmation filter candidate, verified separately once enough forward data exists

what_was_computed: confirmation frequency, time to confirmation, confirmation distance

prior_expectation.first_condition_expected_to_break: S10 (stop-out share) - if confirmation creates no direction information, stop-outs land near 50%
prior_expectation.what_this_experiment_newly_answers: D5.4 showed there is no direction information at the event instant; this asks whether there is any in the price action after it. The two answers are independent.
prior_expectation.structural_novelty: A and C have no profit target, so a failure means trends do not continue rather than that a bracket was mis-sized
